answer: The dawn multiplier is published, charged in velvet, and haven lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 574 identities would post 2984 proofs and burn roughly 86 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
